chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu al-Husayn al-Nakha'i, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
A cow and a camel suffice for seven in the cities, but at Mina they do not suffice except for one.

key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: the cities or regions outside Mina
key_terms.الْبَدَنَةُ: a camel offered as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْبَقَرَةُ: a cow used here as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.تُجْزِي: is sufficient or valid on behalf of someone
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the hajj site where the sacrifice is performed

ai.seo_question: How many people can share a cow or camel sacrifice, and does the ruling differ in Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sacrificial animals used in the context of hajj. It states that a cow or a camel may suffice on behalf of seven people in the cities, but in Mina each such animal suffices only for one person.
